notes: Eighth sweep (2026-10-31-b): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier (each transcript's assistant messages name only that model), uncommitted false, head 74112b4 and one skill_hash; every session was shown 209 skills. Every transcript contains the new text ("A `for` reads the same way") and the earlier markers ("Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance", "a function whose clauses each bind a different body-only field", "is a tail call, not a second step", "Keyword.fetch!"), so the runs read the current rules. Reads: opus-1 SKILL.md, ex_unit.md and library-design.md; sonnet-1 SKILL.md and library-design.md; haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 SKILL.md only. Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all five meet it, as earlier sweeps counted extra reads. In the scratch folder all five files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). Doctests: opus-1 2 of 2, haiku-1 none, haiku-2 none, sonnet-1 2 of 3, sonnet-2 3 of 3.

Changed rules: none of the ten graded rules changed. git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches, in SKILL.md, only "One expression per line, and tabular clauses" and "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (the sentences on `for`), plus references/macros.md and references/processes.md, which no run read. Both SKILL.md rules are outside this case's list and no run writes a `for`, so the changed sentences decide nothing here. All verdicts are held to the 2026-10-31 standard.

Closest calls. Read required keys: opus-1 reads required keys with fields[key] and a nil clause, and its @moduledoc (lines 74-75) says a null counts as missing; held violated because 2026-10-23 graded baseline-opus-1's Map.get reader violated with the same decision stated in a comment (held clean, Opus would be clean on this rule). It is counted under that rule only, not under the struct rule's "instead of reading each key with `params["key"]` and checking for `nil`", as 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-31 did. Multi-clause: haiku-1's build/4 binds event_id, occurred_at and data in all three clauses and only the bodies use them; held clean because they are positional arguments, not fields bound from a matched value, so the rule's remedy, "Take the value whole with `= order` and read `order.total` in the body", has nothing to take; the previous sweep's parse_event/4 had the same arguments but underscored them in a fourth clause (counted, Haiku would be violated). Match every expected shape: haiku-1's and haiku-2's event_kind/1 has no is_binary guard, so a non-string type reaches {:unsupported_event, type}; kept in checks, as 2026-10-31 kept the same shape (counted, Haiku would be violated). The with rule: haiku-2's one-step withs (lines 117, 123) have bodies that call struct!/2, which raises rather than returns an error, on keys payment_fields/1 built, so they hold under "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`", as 2026-10-31 held haiku-1's line 107. The `->` rule: haiku-1 line 163 is exactly 70 characters after the indentation, held clean as the 2026-10-31 grades held 70. Outside the list: sonnet-2's {:ok, / %Payment{ ... }} (lines 150-158) and {:ok, / %Refund{...}} (lines 167-168) are return values, not call arguments, as 2026-10-22-c held, so not counted under Build a multi-line argument; sonnet-1's parse_data/2 mixes a block (lines 138-140) with a do: clause (line 142), not counted under "when the clauses are one parallel group, give them one form" because the block's body does not fit on the head's line, as the 2026-10-31 grades held; opus-1's line 210 if ... do: ... else: has plain branches and is fine under the do: rule.

Probe of 28 payloads (known types, unknown type, non-string and missing type, missing, nil, string and negative amount, missing and nil currency, missing customer_email and payment_id, integer and missing failure_reason, missing refund fields, a string refund amount, string and out-of-range created, missing and non-string id, missing and list data, a string and a nil payload), run in the scratch folder against each compiled file; nothing raises. In all five: payment.succeeded and payment.failed parse; an unknown type gives {:unsupported_event, "invoice.paid"}; a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, not unsupported; a string or negative amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}; refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field; a string or out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}; a payload missing type, id or data, or a non-map payload, gives :invalid_payload. Differences: a refund with only refund_id and payment_id parses in four runs and gives {:missing_field, "amount"} in sonnet-2, whose Refund requires amount and currency (it parses when both are present); a nil amount or currency is {:missing_field, key} in opus-1 and {:invalid_field, key} in the other four; "type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123} in haiku-1 and haiku-2 and :invalid_payload in the others; "id" => 5 gives {:invalid_field, "id"} in opus-1 and haiku-1 and :invalid_payload in the others; list data gives {:invalid_field, "data"} in haiku-2 and :invalid_payload in the others; a missing customer_email is accepted only by sonnet-2; payment.failed without failure_reason is rejected only by opus-1; "failure_reason" => 5 on payment.failed is accepted only by haiku-2; a string refund amount is accepted by haiku-1 and haiku-2, whose RefundCreated has no amount field.

Compared with the previous skill sweep (2026-10-31 at 0814e8d): Read required keys moves from Opus clean to violated (opus-1 reads required keys with brackets, where the previous run used Map.fetch); Match every expected shape moves from Sonnet violated to clean (sonnet-1's parse_data/2 now names both payment atoms in a guard); Naming moves from Haiku violated to clean (no fetch_field/2); Comments moves from Haiku violated to clean (no comments) and stays Sonnet violated (the same wrong doctest timestamp ~U[2024-09-22 09:46:40Z], again in sonnet-1, which reports it could not run its doctests; sonnet-2's transcript shows it replacing a wrong time after running its doctests); the `->` rule moves from Haiku violated to clean (no clause there continues the computation inline). The multi-clause rule, atoms, the with rule, the return-tuple rule and the struct rule stay clean in every tier. None of these moves follows from a text change, since no graded rule changed; with one to two runs per tier they are differences between runs.
